key_insight: Motive provides a motion-centric, gradient-based data-attribution method that isolates and quantifies how individual training/fine-tuning clips influence a video generator's temporal dynamics.
problem_solved: Clarifies which data samples improve or degrade motion in video-generation models by separating temporal dynamics from static appearance, enabling targeted dataset curation and fine-tuning decisions.
method: Compute gradient-based influence scores per clip for a target video-generation model to attribute effects to training/fine-tuning samples.
Use motion-weighted loss masks to isolate temporal dynamics (motion) from static appearance when measuring influence.
Scale the procedure to modern, large, high-quality video datasets and models to identify clips that improve or harm temporal behavior.
impact: Makes it practical to debug and curate datasets for better temporal realism in generated video, helping practitioners prioritize or remove clips that positively or negatively affect motion quality.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input videos → motion-weighted loss mask → gradient attribution → per-clip influence score
Side-by-side video/frame pairs showing examples of improved vs. degraded temporal dynamics after removing/adding high-influence clips
Heatmap overlay on video frames indicating spatial-temporal regions driving attribution
Bar chart ranking fine-tuning clips by positive and negative influence on motion quality
paper_authors: Xindi Wu, Despoina Paschalidou, Jun Gao, Antonio Torralba, Laura Leal-Taixé
